# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_016_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 8

**1** "Any more questions?" she asked when she finished. "Yes — why is the tower built on water?" "Because your life has been saved and will continue to be saved through water. The tower, though, rests on the word of the almighty, glorious Name and is sustained by the Lord's invisible power." **2** "That's remarkable. Who are the six young men doing the building?" "The holy angels of God — the first ones ever created — to whom God gave charge over all his creation: to build it up, expand it, govern it. Through them the tower will be completed." **3** "And the others hauling stones?" "Also holy angels, but under the authority of the six. When the tower is done, they'll all gather around it and celebrate together, praising God for the finished work." **4** "I want to understand," I said, "the rejected stones near the tower, those thrown far away, and the cracked ones." **5** She answered: "The stones rejected but left near the tower — those are people who sinned and want to repent. They haven't been sent far away because they can still be useful if they turn around. **6** If they repent, they'll be strong enough to go into the building — but only if they do it now, while construction is still underway. Once the tower is complete, there's no more room. They'll be shut out." **7** "The cracked ones have faith, but they're entangled in worldly wealth. When trouble comes, their money and business dealings pull them away from the Lord." "When can they become useful?" "When their wealth — which has them under its spell — is stripped away. A round stone can't fit a square space until something is cut from it. The wealthy can't fit God's purpose until their wealth is removed." **8** "What about the white round ones that won't fit?" I pressed. She gave a short sigh. "You keep asking and asking and still don't understand. These are the same: people with faith but with wealth. When pressure comes, they choose their money over their Lord."

---

*PNEUMA note: The short sigh in v.8 is an interpolation to capture the Church's gentle exasperation — the text says "How long will you be foolish?" which implies the same. PNEUMA makes it vivid.*
